messages:
oncall-bot: ALERT: KV cache fanout spike on rope-longctx routes; continuous-batcher saturation detected. Incident INC-2026-489 created. symptoms: 10-15x eviction spikes, batch coalescer latency p95 -> 4.1s, error surge 5xx for high-concurrency tenants

marie-sre: noticed graphs at 22:03 UTC. active_prefixes per host jumped from ~12 -> 340. memory pressure kicked off aggressive LRU evictions causing recompute storm.

leo-runtime: digging in. traces show NTK window stretching + YaRN stride extension created enormous unique KV keys (long prompt prefixes + sliding segments). continuous-batcher is happily grouping all these as separate prefixes, increasing batch assembly time. this smells like the new yarn_adaptive_stride tweak from last deploy.

tess-ml: yes, that change expanded stride to reduce miss rate on very long sessions, but it didn't consider prefix cardinality under high concurrency. steady-state looked fine in perf tests, but we missed the bursty multi-tenant traffic pattern.

sam-cs: customer impact: tenants tenant-alpha and tenant-gamma reported timeouts and slow responses. I'm on with tenant-alpha; they've moved critical flows to a smaller model variant as a stopgap.

olga-enginfra: immediate actions I suggest: 1) set CONT_BATCHER_MAX_PREFIXES=64 (was 1024) 2) temporarily disable yarn_adaptive_stride 3) throttle per-tenant request concurrency on affected routes 4) spin up 3 extra KV shard replicas for hot keys. roll these as a hotpatch to canary first.

leo-runtime: applying canary hotpatch now. running command:

```
# canary hotpatch
kubectl -n inference set env deployment/continuous-batcher CONT_BATCHER_MAX_PREFIXES=64 YARN_ADAPTIVE_STRIDE=0
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/continuous-batcher --record
```

marie-sre: saw canary logs within 90s. eviction rate down ~9x, active_prefixes on canary ~30. p95 dropped back toward 210ms on canary.

tess-ml: confirm on canary: cache hit_rate slightly dipped (0.68 -> 0.61) but latency improved. acceptable tradeoff for now. we should monitor for increased token compute due to prefix rebuilds.

ria-prodeng: coordinate staggered rollout. we'll do 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% with 7m holds. prepare rollback script if any host shows >1.5x baseline 5xxs.

leo-runtime: rolling out wave 1 -> 10%.

marie-sre: after 30m into rollout, cluster-wide metrics show stabilized eviction curve. some prefix rebuild noise expected; overall error rate back to baseline.

sam-cs: updated customers: tenant-alpha acknowledged improvement, tenant-gamma still seeing intermittent tails; offered routing to dedicated capacity if needed.

olga-enginfra: note: rebalancing KV shards added load to control-plane; keep an eye on kube-scheduler logs. I submitted a quick fix to reduce shard rebalance aggressiveness.

tess-ml: long-term fixes proposed: - revert/adjust yarn_adaptive_stride with a per-tenant cardinality cap - implement per-prefix aging weight to avoid long-tail prefix retention - add synthetic burst test in CI to simulate multi-tenant longctx churn

marie-sre: filing follow-up ticket INFRA-1214 to track code rollback + additional tests. linking dashboards: https://internal.redwood/dashboards/kv-fanout and rollout logs: https://internal.redwood/logs/continuous-batcher/2193456789

noah-oncall: taking handoff for the midnight shift. summary for next on-call: hotpatch applied and rolled to 100%, canary metrics showed p95 improvement from 4.1s -> ~220ms, eviction rate down ~90%, affected tenants partially recovered but monitor tenant-gamma tails. outstanding risks: prefix rebuild compute spikes and control-plane load from KV shard changes.

noah-oncall: I'll keep the hotpatch until the ml/runtime team lands a refined yarn stride with per-tenant limits or a tested revert. assigned INFRA-1214 to leo-runtime and tess-ml.

marie-sre: added notes to postmortem doc: timeline, root cause (NTK/YaRN extension -> prefix cardinality explosion), immediate mitigations (max_prefixes cap, disable adaptive stride, per-tenant throttles, KV replica spin-up), customer impact summary, and long-term action items.

leo-runtime: snippet from canary after patch:

```
[2026-03-16T00:11:02Z] INFO batcher: prefixes=28 batch_assembly_ms=12 eviction_rate=0.001
[2026-03-16T00:11:02Z] INFO kv: hit_rate=0.62 prefix_rebuilds=7
```

marie-sre: final note: no indications of security/data integrity issues. this is a performance/regression incident. will prepare short postmortem and notify stakeholders.
